To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

happy music without words induced stronger positive emotions and recruited more brain regions involved in affective processing, compared to happy music with words, whereas sad music was processed differently, depending on the presence of words.

1) happy music with lyrics induced weaker positive emotions than happy instrumental music; 2) sad music with lyrics activated the parahippoccampal gyrus and the amygdala more than sad instrumental music; 3) happy music with and without lyrics activated different brain regions, with happy music with lyrics activating only the auditory cortex, and happy music without lyrics activating both the auditory cortex and the limbic system.
